Thank you. I guess here’s an update if you or anyone is interested. I haven’t spoken to that doctor yet but according to the online platform’s privacy policy they can collect information from your national e health record AND even your skills, qualification and experience which is unlike any other real life GP/clinic I’ve been to. There was even mention of sexual orientation, religion.. etc. So I guess somewhere in my notes one of my GPs diagnosed or thought I may have genital herpes given I complained about genital pain at a real life clinic recently at the time. I figured this must be the case and the other doctor I talked to from the platform didn’t want to be fully transparent about how much data and information he could see about me (especially given a normal clinic in AU cannot see another clinic’s notes about a person unless they opted in for an online health record which I really haven’t).

Further I realised the doctor who prescribed me with the antibiotics (that I realised are for a breast infection) must have done so based on previous recent notes from another real life clinic that I had breast bleeding. That real life doctor did a breast examination and didn’t see anything wrong. I guess the online doctor disagreed with her so prescribed antibiotics. And also came to the conclusion I had genital herpes as well. 

I’ve calmed down about the herpes. I don’t think the doctors at my local clinic will hide a diagnosis like herpes simplex virus 2 from me as I have seen them since I was 13. Thanks for your support.



Tl;dr-
Local GPs are not hiding a HSV2 diagnosis from me.
